name: backup_decrypt
description: Decrypt an encrypted iOS backup (a Finder or iTunes backup made with Encrypt local backup, iOS 13 or later) with the library iphone_backup_decrypt, pinned in requires/ with hashes, from a password in a file the job was given. The tool implements no cryptography and guesses nothing about the key bag: the library opens the backup in a child process of this tool (its time is bounded, and a stop ends it with whatever it started). Output under $OUT/backup_decrypt-<id>/decrypted: Manifest.db decrypted, one decrypted file per Manifest row of a file at <first two digits of its id>/<file id> (no name of the phone is used for a file, so a hostile Manifest path writes nowhere), every file mode 0600, created exclusively and never replaced, and DECRYPTED.json, the banner that says this is a decrypted copy of what a backup kept, not the phone, not an acquisition, and not a backup directory (Manifest.plist is not carried over). The whole account, one line per Manifest row with what became of it, is a result file the answer names (the inline page is a prefix). `password_ref` is a path to a regular file of mode 0600 (no link, pipe, device or directory; 1 to 4096 bytes; one trailing newline dropped) given to the job as an input; this process only looks at it, and the child reads it and hands the text to the library in memory. The password is on no command line, in no environment variable, on neither output channel of the child (both go nowhere), in no path, JSON key, error or file; a library exception is reported by class name only; no key bag, class key or manifest key is printed (Manifest.plist's key material is a presence and a length). The manifest declares secret_output required: every job of the tool is a secret output, and the tool refuses to run outside a job run as secret output (SECRET_OUTPUT=1), as JSON, before anything is made. Outcomes, told apart: verified (the decrypted Manifest.db opens as SQLite and every row of a file was decrypted to the length the Manifest records as its Size; directory and link rows have no blob), partial (the rows that are not are counted by outcome: blob_missing, size_mismatch, decrypted_size_unknown, backend_error, ambiguous_selection, refused_id, duplicate_id, not_copied_max_bytes, not_attempted_max_files, not_attempted, write_failed, unknown_kind_not_decrypted for a row whose flags are not file, directory or link), wrong_secret (the backup is of the shape this tool knows and the backend raised its IncorrectPassphraseError; any other exception of the backend while opening or unlocking is outcome failed with the exception class, never read as a wrong password), secret_unavailable (no usable password file), unsupported_format (Manifest.plist missing, unreadable, not IsEncrypted true, without BackupKeyBag or ManifestKey, or Manifest.db plain: nothing is attempted) and backend_unavailable. Verified is not a claim that a file's content is what the phone held: a file id is a locator and the Manifest records no digest of content. The backend selects a file by `relativePath = ? AND domain LIKE ? AND flags = 1 ORDER BY domain, relativePath LIMIT 1` (iphone_backup_decrypt 0.11.2, as reported by a reader of its source; not read by the author), so a row can be decrypted from another row's blob (domains equal up to case, a `_` or `%` in a domain, a collation that equates two paths, a pattern over SQLite's length limit). Before every file the child runs that query with LIMIT 2 on a copy of the decrypted map; a row it does not return alone, or whose query fails, is not decrypted and is listed as ambiguous_selection. The library has been exercised here only through a stand-in for its documented calls (EncryptedBackup, save_manifest_file, extract_file); it has not been run against a real backup. It does not decrypt anything but an iOS backup directory, does not break or guess a password, does not read the keychain, and a backup made before iOS 13 is not claimed. Limits: max_files, max_bytes (of the encrypted blobs it would decrypt), max_seconds (the tool's own clock, of which the child has 78 %), at most 4,000,000 rows of the map are read.  A process that the child (this tool's own process, which runs the library) or the library left running after it exited (one that holds a file the tool keeps, in the tool's process group or in a session of its own, or one that holds no descriptor and writes by name) is stopped, killed and reaped by the shared process block's settle() before the decrypted files are read, sized and hashed; one found, or a host where the absence of one cannot be proven (not Linux, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER refused), makes the answer at most partial (program_group.left_behind, program_group.unproven and a line in problems and status_basis), and the decrypted files and the counts are then what the leftover had written when it was ended. A refusal carries no program_group. A process that is no descendant of the program (started through a service manager) is not found.

backup.description: The encrypted backup directory (Manifest.plist, Manifest.db and the blobs): a directory in the job's inputs

password_ref.description: A path to a regular file of mode 0600 holding the password, given to the job as an input (1 to 4096 bytes; one trailing newline dropped). Never the password itself

max_files.description: The most files decrypted (default 200000, at most 2000000); the rows after it are not_attempted_max_files

max_bytes.description: The most encrypted-blob bytes decrypted in all (default 4 GiB, at most 4 TiB); a blob that would pass it is not_copied_max_bytes

max_seconds.description: The tool's own clock (default 480, at most 540; the manifest's timeout is 600): the child has 78 % of it for the key derivation and the files, the tool the rest to read the result and write the answer; the answer says partial and where it stopped

limit.description: Rows in the inline answer (default 200, and at most 1 MiB of rows); the whole account is the result file the answer names
